requirement:
Extend the existing URL-shortener service to support an optional custom alias
when creating a link. Analyze the change against docs/01-business-requirement.md,
docs/02-requirement-analysis.md, docs/03-engineering-design.md, and the current
codebase.

Keep the existing stack, default generated-code behavior, redirect behavior,
analytics behavior, and API response contract compatible for callers that do
not provide an alias. Identify the required request/schema, service, persistence,
migration, API documentation, and test changes. Surface decisions that need
human input, including alias character rules, length limits, reserved values,
and duplicate-alias behavior. Do not add link expiration or other features.

Return a structured draft with affected requirements and components, assumptions,
open questions, risks, ordered tasks with dependencies, tests, and acceptance
checks. Mark it pending human review; do not imply the feature has been approved
or implemented.
summary: Assess an optional custom-alias enhancement to the existing URL-shortener without silently approving it.
functional_requirements: Keep generated codes working when a caller omits a custom alias.
If approved, accept an optional alias when creating a link and preserve existing redirects and analytics.
quality_requirements: Preserve backward compatibility for existing API clients.
Enforce alias uniqueness safely under concurrent creation requests.
Document and test validation and duplicate-alias behavior.
assumptions: Alias support is a proposed enhancement, not part of the currently accepted baseline.
No expiration behavior is included in this request.
open_questions: What characters, length bounds, case sensitivity, and reserved aliases are allowed?
What response should a duplicate alias produce?
Is a database migration required, or can the existing unique code column support aliases?
risks: Unapproved alias rules could create incompatible API behavior.
A migration or uniqueness implementation could invalidate existing mappings if not tested against current data.

human_review.notes:
Accept the proposed custom-alias scope with these rules: aliases must be 3–16
lowercase ASCII letters, digits, or hyphens; must start and end with a letter
or digit; and uppercase input is rejected. Reserve api, health, metrics, docs,
redoc, and openapi.json. A duplicate alias returns HTTP 409 using the standard
error response. Keep aliases optional and preserve generated codes and the
existing response contract when omitted. First verify whether the current
unique code column supports the rules; make a migration only if required.
This accepts the requirement and rules for implementation, not the completed
feature or its test results.
